review_candidates.description: Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191-member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The IFRC is scaling up a national society‑led response centred on community engagement, surveillance, and infection control, supported by an emergency appeal. Red Cross volunteers are mobilized in affected areas to conduct door‑to‑door awareness, counter misinformation, encourage early care‑seeking, and support safe and dignified burials, key to breaking transmission. At the same time, the IFRC is coordinating closely with governments and partners, strengthening cross border preparedness, mobilizing resources and surge capacity, and supporting logistics, infection prevention control, and community-based surveillance to contain the outbreak and reduce regional spread. The Ebola outbreak, declared mid‑May 2026, is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, with hundreds of suspected cases and hundreds of deaths reported across Ituri, South Kivu and North Kivu provinces. It began with clusters of unexplained deaths in early May and is spreading in a context of weak health systems, population movement, insecurity, and community mistrust, which together increase the risk of sustained transmission and cross‑border spread to neighboring countries such as Uganda and South Sudan. The absence of an approved vaccine or specific treatment for this strain makes the outbreak particularly complex and heightens the urgency of rapid containment. The Readiness and Preparedness Officer provides technical coordination for Ebola preparedness, readiness, and anticipatory action initiatives across DRC and other cluster countries (Burundi, Congo and Rwanda). The Readiness and Preparedness Officer reports to the Deputy Operations Manager. Job Purpose Reporting to the Deputy Operations Manager, the Readiness and Preparedness Officer supports the National Society and IFRC in strengthening operational readiness, contingency planning, early warning and early action systems, cross-border preparedness, community-based surveillance, and response capacities to minimize the impact of Ebola outbreaks. The role ensures that preparedness interventions are evidence-based, aligned with IFRC frameworks and national strategies, and contribute to strengthening institutional and community resilience to epidemic threats. The officer works closely with health, PGI, CEA, PMER, logistics, and external partners to ensure preparedness measures are functional, tested, and ready for activation. the effective planning, coordination, and implementation of the operation in line with IFRC standards and the Emergency Response Framework. Job Duties And Responsibilities Ebola Readiness and Preparedness Lead the planning, implementation, and monitoring of Ebola preparedness and readiness activities under the Emergency Appeal and preparedness programmes. Support National Society branches and volunteers in strengthening Ebola preparedness capacities. Ensure contingency plans, preparedness action plans, and standard operating procedures are up to date and regularly reviewed. Coordinate simulation exercises, drills, and readiness assessments to test operational capacities. Support the establishment and maintenance of surge mechanisms, standby rosters, and emergency deployment systems. Monitor readiness indicators and preparedness benchmarks and recommend corrective actions where gaps are identified. Epidemic Anticipatory Action and Early Warning Coordinate inputs and contributions to the Federation-wide Appeal, ensuring timely, accurate, and high-quality submissions. Support the development and operationalization of Early Warning Early Action (EWEA) systems for Ebola and other epidemic-prone diseases. Contribute to the design and testing of Anticipatory Action frameworks and Early Action Protocols. Monitor epidemiological trends, risk indicators, and contextual factors that may trigger preparedness actions. Promote integration of Ebola preparedness within broader multi-hazard disaster risk management approaches. Strengthen linkages between epidemic preparedness, climate-related risks, and community resilience initiatives. Cross-Border and Regional Coordination Support coordination with neighbouring National Societies and IFRC delegations on Ebola preparedness initiatives. Strengthen cross-border information sharing, joint planning, and preparedness mechanisms. Support harmonization of community engagement, surveillance, risk communication, and referral systems across borders. In the absence of the Dep Ops Manager participate in regional preparedness platforms and technical working groups. Coordinate with government authorities, WHO, UNICEF, and other partners involved in Ebola preparedness. Job Duties And Responsibilities (continued) NS Capacity Strengthening Organize and facilitate trainings for NS/IFRC staff and volunteers on: Ebola readiness and preparedness to respond Community-based surveillance Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Safe and Dignified Burials (SDB) Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA) Support branch-level preparedness planning and implementation Facilitate peer learning and knowledge exchange among National Societies Support Preparedness for Effective Response (PER) assessments and action planning Community Readiness and Risk Communication Support community preparedness initiatives aimed at increasing awareness and reducing Ebola transmission risks. Work closely with CEA teams to strengthen community feedback systems and address misinformation, rumors, and concerns. Ensure preparedness interventions are community-centred and inclusive. Support the development and dissemination of preparedness messaging and community engagement tools. Information Management, Reporting and Learning Track preparedness activities and maintain readiness monitoring tools. Prepare regular progress reports, situation updates, and technical briefs. Support preparedness assessments, after-action reviews, and lessons learned exercises. Contribute to donor reporting and operational updates. Document best practices and support knowledge management initiatives. Education Required University degree in Public Health, Epidemiology, Disaster Risk Management, Health Sciences, Community Development, International Relations, or related field Preferred IMPACT training or equivalent knowledge. Experience Required Minimum 3-5 years of experience in disaster management, public health emergency preparedness, or epidemic preparedness Experience supporting preparedness and response operations Experience working with government health authorities, humanitarian organizations, or the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement Experience in capacity strengthening and training delivery Experience in contingency planning and preparedness assessments. Preferred Previous Ebola outbreak preparedness or response experience Experience supporting cross-border health emergency preparedness initiatives Knowledge of IFRC PER, EWEA, and Anticipatory Action frameworks Knowledge, Skills and Languages Required Strong understanding of epidemic readiness, preparedness and response Knowledge of Ebola prevention, surveillance, IPC, and community engagement approaches Familiarity with preparedness planning, PER, contingency planning, and readiness assessment tools Strong analytical and reporting skills Excellent coordination, networking, and stakeholder engagement skills Experience facilitating trainings and workshops Ability to work in multicultural and high-pressure environments Strong planning, organization, and problem-solving skills Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications or IFRC digital tools or related Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and digital data management platforms, including IFRC systems and tools, with the ability to effectively utilize technology for planning, reporting, information management, and operational readiness Good written and spoken English and English Preferred Specialized training in epidemic preparedness, outbreak management, IPC, RCCE, or public health emergencies Good command of another IFRC official language (Spanish or Arabic) Knowledge of Congolese National Languages Competencies, Values and Comments VALUES: Respect for diversity; Integrity; Professionalism; Accountability CORE COMPETENCIES: Communication; Collaboration and Teamwork; National Society relations; Strategic orientation; Communication; Teamwork

review_candidates.description: Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference within life sciences, diagnostics and biotechnology? At Molecular Devices, one of Danaher’s 15+ operating companies, our work saves lives—and we’re all united by a shared commitment to innovate for tangible impact. You’ll thrive in a culture of belonging where you and your unique viewpoint matter. And by harnessing Danaher’s system of continuous improvement, you help turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life. Join Molecular Devices and help drive scientific discovery for life science customers in academia, biotech, pharma, and government. Our automated and AI-enabled technology empowers researchers to tackle complex questions and gain deep insights, accelerating the development of safer, more effective therapeutics. As part of our team—rooted in collaboration, authenticity, and innovation—you’ll ultimately contribute to groundbreaking science that enhances lives globally and shapes a healthier future for all. Job Summary We are looking for a Field Service Engineer based in the Netherlands and able to work remote with technical support across the central region. This position reports to the EU Central Field Service Manager and is part of the Field Service team and requires weekly travels. The Field Service Engineer (EU Central) will provide professional field service support for Molecular Devices products, performing to agreed service levels for all customers within the assigned territory. This will include installations, service repair and preventative maintenance for Molecular Devices instruments. You will join a team of dedicated Field Service Professionals, contributing to our success by utilizing critical thinking to analyze and solve problems, implementing suitable solutions. You will consistently provide timely, high quality, on-site troubleshooting and maintenance services for high-performance bio-analytical measurement and research instrumentation. Key Responsibilities Become proficient in the support of our world class products so that you can provide consistent, world class services and support to our customers. Take responsibility for assigned customer service inquiries, repairs, installations, preventative maintenance and OQ schedules. Support our customer to fast-track scientific discoveries, as you help us pave the way for advanced disease detection, drug discovery, and therapeutic development, crucial for improving human health and wellness. The Essential Requirements Of The Job Include Minimum 3 years of Industry relevant work experience in a similar role Good mechanical, electronics, and electrical experience and knowledge of assembly level fault detection and testing (Instrument specific training will be provided). Applicants must be customer focussed, able to communicate well and able to work independently, taking ownership of issues from beginning to end. Travel, Motor Vehicle Record & Physical/Environment Requirements Ability to travel – Minimum of 80% utilization. Regular overnight travel will be required, within primarily the Benelux Region. With occasional travel to other locations for training and to assist other service teams, as the need arises. Must have a valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record It would be a plus if you also possess previous experience in: IT, computer and network management Cellular Imaging Products diagnostics and repairs Working in a Lab environment Molecular Devices, a Danaher operating company, offers a broad array of comprehensive, competitive benefit programs that add value to our lives. Whether it’s a health care program or paid time off, our programs contribute to life beyond the job. Check out our benefits at Danaher Benefits Info. At Molecular Devices we believe in designing a better, more sustainable workforce. We recognize the benefits of flexible, remote working arrangements for eligible roles and are committed to providing enriching careers, no matter the work arrangement. This position is eligible for a remote work arrangement in which you can work remotely from your home. Additional information about this remote work arrangement will be provided by your interview team. Explore the flexibility and challenge that working for Molecular Devices can provide. Join our winning team today. Together, we’ll accelerate the real-life impact of tomorrow’s science and technology. We partner with customers across the globe to help them solve their most complex challenges, architecting solutions that bring the power of science to life. For more information, visit www.danaher.com.
